output.brief:
The cause is almost certainly contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique or the new pads. Northfield Motor Services refilled 11 of the Eastgate vans (those not using a fresh drum) from an old bulk drum that had lost its cap and absorbed water. Two of those vans were tested on 24 Sep: their fluid boiled at about 150°C against 255°C for fresh fluid. That is low enough for the fluid to vaporise on long descents and make the pedal go soft. All 11 vans that complained are on that list. The two Northfield vans serviced from a new drum have no complaints. The same drivers drove other vans on Upper Wend, 141 days in all, with no brake reports. Pads from the same Tessaro batches on the Calder Road vans produced no complaints. Upper Wend only exposed a fault already in the vans.

What to do this week: pull every van Northfield serviced before 10 Sep, test the fluid and renew it from sealed stock. Prioritise the 11 that complained and also check the rest, since Northfield's own recommendation of a recheck went unanswered. Drop the written warnings and the retraining, which would punish people for reporting a real fault. Hold off on changing pad supplier. The squeal reports may only reflect fresh pads. I'm fairly confident in this.
